messages:
Alex: Heads-up, we just got an escalation from support — customer reports p95/p99 latency regressions after they switched to `int8` quantization for gptx-6. They say tail latency tripled on some routes. @oncall-bot flagged it as SEV-2.
Sara: link to support thread? can we see repro steps + request IDs? :eyes:
support-bot: Customer ticket #C-4821: 'After enabling int8_profile=aggressive, median latency ok but p95/p99 increased 2-3x on chat-generation route. No errors, just slower tokens.' Attached logs + example request id: `req-20260315-22a`
Alex: copying the customer's repro here (sanitized):
```
POST /v1/generate
Authorization: Bearer <redacted>
body: {
  model: "gptx-6",
  quant_profile: "int8_aggressive",
  prompt: "<few-shot chat>",
  max_tokens: 512,
  stream: false
}
```
They tested 100 requests, warm cache, batch=1. p50 ~ 120ms, p95 went from ~260ms (fp16) to ~800ms (int8).
Sam: interesting. Does the runtime fall back on any kernels? ask customer for `runtime_debug=true` logs to see if there are fallback messages.
Alex: I pulled our telemetry for that model variant in the last 24h — we see a small cluster of spikes coincident with their rollout: p95 jumped from 280ms -> 760ms, cpu-side time also increased.
Lisa: Could be quantization calibration causing extra dequant/requant overhead or different kernel path that doesn't support fused attention and ends up using slower kernels. Any config that would force fallback to `fp16`?
Mike: There's a known issue where `int8_aggressive` triggers a per-layer fallback when calibration variance > threshold; that path currently does fine correctness-wise but forces a non-optimized matmul kernel that is slower. Not supposed to hit for gptx-6, but maybe data distribution changed.
Alex: steps I want to run quickly: 1) reproduce in canary with same quant profile and prompt 2) run `--kernel-trace` to list selected kernels 3) try `int8_moderate` or `calibrate=true` with longer calibration set 4) if immediate mitigation needed, pin to `fp16` or `int8_safe` variant via routing.
Sam: I repro'd locally with the customer's prompt (using env=staging). Observed similar p95 bump. Kernel trace shows: `attention: fallback_unfused_matmul_v2`, `ffn: int8_matmul_dequant_requant` — both slower than fused kernels.
Lisa: That matches the hypothesis. Can you paste the kernel trace snippet?
Sam: paste:```
KERNEL_SELECT: attention -> fallback_unfused_matmul_v2 (latency 1.8x)
KERNEL_SELECT: ffn -> int8_deq_requant_matmul (latency 2.1x)
CALIBRATION: layer 10 variance high -> fallback enabled
```
Alex: thanks. So calibration variance on some layers toggles fallback, which increases per-token cost and hits tails when token counts vary.
Mike: short-term mitigation options:
- Route affected customers to `gptx-6-fp16` or `gptx-6-int8_safe` variant that uses per-layer safe configs. (Lowest risk)
- Change quant_profile from `int8_aggressive` -> `int8_moderate` (should reduce fallbacks)
- Force per-request header `x-inference-prefer-fp16: true` (if they accept slightly higher median cost)
Alex: I suggested in customer ticket: rollback to `fp16` while we investigate. They want to avoid cost increase. Can we offer `int8_moderate` as compromise?
Sara: also add a quick canary rollback on the gateway: update routing rule for that org id -> variant `gptx-6-int8_safe` for 100% traffic. I can push that.
Alex: do it and note in ticket. Sam, can you add debug instrumentation to measure per-layer fallback counts for that variant? We need a histogram for fallback occurrences per request.
Sam: on it. I'll add: `quant.fallback_count` metric + `quant.fallback_layers` tag and wire into console dashboards.
Lisa: long-term: we should improve calibration sampling and detection so we don't trigger fallback on borderline variance. Also need faster int8 fused kernels for attention if feasible. I'll raise an eng task.
Mike: FYI, there was an upstream cuBLAS kernel regression in a vendor release that made some matmul variants slower for certain shapes; worth checking the GPU driver + libcudnn versions customer uses.
Alex: good call. Support, can you confirm customer's infra: gpu type, driver, runtime?
support-bot: Customer provided environment: AWS g5.2xlarge (A10G), CUDA 12.1, driver 535.86, container image `redwood/runtime:2026-02-10`
Sam: that's similar to our staging. So less likely driver-specific.
Alex: immediate action list (short):
1) Sara: route org=acme -> `gptx-6-int8_safe` now. (PR + changelog)
2) Sam: add `quant.fallback_count` metric and enable kernel-trace on canary for 2 hours.
3) Lisa: create ENG ticket to investigate calibration thresholds + kernel selection for int8_aggressive (assign to eng-ml).
4) Mike: confirm if any recent vendor kernel regressions for our HW/shape combos.
5) Support: update customer ticket with mitigation and ask if they'd accept `int8_moderate` as test.
Sam: started a canary test. Early results: fallback_count spikes on layer 10 & 11, 37% of requests have >=1 fallback, those requests correspond to p99 bucket.
Alex: that's actionable. For mitigation, I'm going to whitelist `int8_aggressive` only for requests with `avg_seq_len < 64` until we fix it. Add a routing rule that splits by inferred seq_len.
Lisa: note: we need policy config for seq_len-based routing in the console; I can add a temporary rule in routing policies.
Sam: reproduced p95 improvement after switching canary to `int8_moderate`: p95 dropped from ~780ms -> 320ms, p50 unchanged. So `int8_moderate` looks safe.
Alex: excellent. Can we document a recommended flow for customers: (1) run calibration with a representative dataset (N>=500 sequences), (2) start with `int8_moderate`, (3) enable `int8_aggressive` only after monitoring fallback_count for 24h.
Lisa: I'll draft a KB article and a console warning when customers select `int8_aggressive` that shows potential tail risk and suggests calibration sample size.
Mike: one more note: if fallback_count is due to outlier tokens (unusual activation distribution), we might minimize with prefix caching and prompt normalization. Worth trying as a micro-optimization for customers that need aggressive quant.
Alex: tickets and PRs: Sara -> routing PR #4783, Sam -> metrics PR #5125, Lisa -> ENG task #ENG-1259. I'll update the customer and mark SEV-2 until we confirm stable p99.
support-bot: Customer updated: ok to try `int8_moderate` for 24h test.
Alex: Great. After 24h, we'll aggregate telemetry and decide on permanent rollback or root-cause fix. Thanks all. :white_check_mark:
Sam: logging note for postmortem: include kernel traces, calibration snapshots, and sample prompts that trigger fallback.
Lisa: adding that to ENG-1259.
Mike: I'll parallel-check vendor changelogs, will post findings here.
Alex: closing the loop: if anyone sees residual p99 > 2x baseline after mitigation, @oncall-bot escalate to SEV-1.
oncall-bot: Acknowledged. Monitoring alert rule updated for `model:gptx-6` p99 delta > 2x baseline.
